body:
Alex Martinez: quick q for the demo app (PR-193): should we hit the OpenAI-compat endpoint or use the native Redwood SDK?

Alex Martinez: i keep seeing customers ask “do you support OpenAI SDK drop-in” so compat feels like the path of least resistance. but we also want to show off structured output + tool calling + retries in a way that’s super clean.

Monica Patel: depends what we’re optimizing for.
- OpenAI-compat: best for “swap the base_url and go”. less code, instantly relatable.
- Native SDK: we can demonstrate Redwood-specific features + better defaults (stream handling, retry policy, request ids, tracing hooks).

Renee Sullivan: demo talk track wise, SEs keep wanting to say “you don’t need to rewrite your stack”. the compat route supports that story.

Monica Patel: yup. but some of the newer goodies (esp the structured output helper + typed tool schemas) are nicer in the native SDK. compat means we’ll re-implement a bit of glue.

Alex Martinez: what’s the risk of compat endpoint drift? i don’t want the demo to break if OpenAI SDK changes some param naming or they add strict validation.

Monica Patel: that’s the main drawback. we don’t control their client release cadence. also TS SDK in particular has had breaking changes.

Monica Patel: if we go compat, we should pin openai package versions in both python + node and treat upgrades like a deliberate chore.

Renee Sullivan: also: in the demo we show Console dashboards w/ token-level breakdown. do we lose any metadata if we come via compat?

Monica Patel: we still get usage + latency obviously. but native SDK lets us standardize headers + tags (e.g. `x-redwood-demo-scenario`) without weird workarounds.

Elliot Price: from docs enablement standpoint: the “drop-in compat” snippet is a *huge* win. it reduces the amount of explaining we do in a live demo.

Alex Martinez: could we do a hybrid? like: default flow uses compat to prove drop-in, and then a toggle / advanced tab uses native to show the extra controls.

Renee Sullivan: i like that. also gives us a backup path: if OpenAI client does something weird, we can flip to native and still run the scenarios.

Markus Klein: +1 hybrid, but please keep the live demo steps minimal. SEs will not want to explain two clients in 30 mins.

Markus Klein: can we do: app uses native internally for stability, but we show an “equivalent drop-in snippet” on-screen (copy/paste) for the audience?

Alex Martinez: that’s a good point. show the snippet != run the snippet.

Simran Kaur: for enterprise folks: the compat story is fine, but questions come up around auth + org/project scoping. native SDK makes it easier to show least-privilege key usage + project separation.

Monica Patel: also tool calling: compat will work, but the experience can be awkward b/c of how OpenAI represents tools. native SDK can present a cleaner “tool registry” example.

Renee Sullivan: what about streaming? i’ve seen OpenAI client streaming APIs differ across versions. don’t want SEs debugging event formats mid-call.

Monica Patel: exactly. native gives us consistent streaming surface and we can match our own “known-good” examples.

Alex Martinez: ok proposal:
1) demo app runs on native Redwood SDK (python + ts) for stability + tagging.
2) README includes a short OpenAI-compat “drop-in” snippet (base_url + api_key) for both languages.
3) talk track: AE/SE says “we’re compatible w/ OpenAI clients” and shows snippet, but we don’t depend on it live.

Elliot Price: +1. i can make sure the snippet is prominent and we have the pinned versions called out.

Monica Patel: works for me. i’ll add a note to pin versions in the repo (`openai==...`, `openai@...`) and we can set renovate rules to not auto-bump.

Renee Sullivan: also please add the scenario tag header so Console filters work (“structured-output”, “tool-calling”, “fallback-routing”). makes the dashboard tour cleaner.

Monica Patel: yep, native SDK can set that cleanly. i’ll wire it as an optional config.

RedwoodBot: :memo: Action items captured
- Monica Patel: update demo app to use native SDK + add scenario tagging header
- Elliot Price: add OpenAI-compat snippets + pinned versions to README / enablement docs
- Alex Martinez: update talk track language to “OpenAI-compatible, plus deeper native controls when you want them”

Markus Klein: :thumbsup: please also call out in the README: “for demos, we run native to avoid client version drift.” this will save SEs time.

Alex Martinez: done. i’ll post back when the PR is up.
